findings.title: Light/dark values swapped for embedded-post username link
findings.body: The rule for `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` (the bold username shown in the expanded "in reply to" post above a reply) used to be `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new line is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` — the light-theme argument changed from 30% to 70%, and the dark-theme argument is 30%. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original percentage as the first (light) argument and mirrors it for dark (e.g. `.username.new-user a` in this same file correctly uses 70% light / 30% dark). Here the two appear swapped: light themes now render this prominent bold link at primary+70% (light gray on a light background) and dark themes get secondary+30% (dark gray on a dark background), both low-contrast. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light/dark values swapped for .custom-message-length on mobile
findings.body: In mobile/modal.scss the `.custom-message-length` hint (character counter in the flag modal) was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss line 94) for the same class correctly kept 70% for light and added 30% for dark. On mobile the arguments are reversed: light themes get primary+30% (much darker than the intended dimmed hint) and dark themes get secondary+70% (much lighter), i.e. the de-emphasis is inverted in both themes. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` to match desktop.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness for .topic-map h3 changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: In mobile/topic-post.scss, `.topic-map h3` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The desktop version of the same rule (desktop/topic-post.scss line 321) kept 20% for light and added 80% for dark, which is the pattern this PR follows everywhere else. On mobile light themes the topic-map heading text is now significantly lighter than before, and dark themes get 50% instead of the mirrored 80%, so mobile and desktop render the same element differently. Unless the light-theme change was intentional, this should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness for .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: In desktop/user.scss, `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme color (30% -> 50%, i.e. lighter) rather than only adding a dark variant. The parallel rule for usernames in common/base/user.scss (`.user-small .username a`, also originally 30%) was correctly converted to 30% light / 70% dark, so this looks like an accidental change. The same edit was made in mobile/user.scss line 497. If intentional (to match the sibling `.title` at 50%), it should be called out, since the PR's stated purpose is only adding dark-theme variants; otherwise use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness for .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: In mobile/user.scss, `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which changes rendering on light themes (the name becomes lighter) instead of only adding the dark-theme variant. Other 30% instances in this PR (e.g. common/base/user.scss `.user-small .name`) were converted to 30% light / 70% dark. The same change exists in desktop/user.scss line 522. If not a deliberate light-theme restyle, this should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Missed scale-color instance: category badge-notification still light-theme only
findings.body: In _topic-list.scss, `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. Every other `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` occurrence in this file (th, td, topic-excerpt, etc.) was converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, so this one appears to have been overlooked. On dark themes the new-topic count badge on the categories list will get the light-theme treatment (an already-light $primary lightened a further 50%, near-white) instead of the dimmed secondary-based color used elsewhere, making it visually inconsistent with the surrounding converted text.
